subject: Media Literacy
title: Loaded Language
description: A micro-lesson that makes Loaded Language usable.

hook.text: 'Freedom fighters' or 'terrorists'? Same people. Different word. Completely different reaction.

buildup.text: Loaded language uses words with strong emotional connotations to influence perception before analysis.

discovery.text: 'Tax relief' frames taxes as a burden. 'Revenue' frames them as a resource. The framing shapes the debate.

twist.text: Loaded language is nearly invisible because we process word connotations before we process logic.

climax.text: Replacing one word in a headline can flip public opinion. Language isn't neutral — it's a battleground.

punchline.text: The word you choose has already made the argument.

quiz.question: Why is loaded language effective?
options: We process emotional connotations before logic
